A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRPO-MA study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are readable and matchable despite restructuring and additions.

before.justification: v3 reports original training and evaluation results across math, code, vision, and simulated manipulation, together with empirical diagnostics and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds a Qwen3 comparison, reward-variance measurements, and a temperature ablation.

M1.justification: The same thought/answer sampling, reward averaging, group normalization, clipped policy objectives, and KL penalty are retained in v3 Section 4.1 and v4 Section 3.4. The shared-context formulation and joint-expectation notation generalize and clarify the analysis without establishing an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets and tasks are retained. GSM8K and HumanEval already appear in v3 Appendix G.6 and Table 11; v4 redisplays their results in Table 2 and retains them in Table 14. New diagnostics reuse existing math, detection, and trajectory tasks.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds GRPO-T16A1 to the Qwen3-4B math comparison, previously limited to T4A1 and GRPO-MA-T4A4. Its code participation is unresolved: v4 prints a score but says that run was omitted. Other evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged; Appendix C.6's method mapping is not an additional evaluation.

E3.justification: v4 adds Pass@1 to AIME/LiveBench evaluation using the retained 100 generations, a Qwen3 T16A1 configuration, a temperature-0.1 trajectory control, and a fixed-prefix reward diagnostic. Appendix D.7 corrects the printed ANLS summation indexing. Existing splits and training hyperparameters are retained; these changes do not establish rerunning existing results.

E4.justification: New Appendices G.6–G.7 directly test whether rewards vary appreciably under a fixed thought and whether lowering sampling temperature explains branching's benefits. These targeted diagnostics supplement the retained answer-count ablation, covariance analysis, inconsistency analysis, case studies, and training curves.

E5.justification: Appendix G.6 newly specifies estimating within-thought variability from four completions and reporting mean variance and range. This concerns conditional reward variability, not uncertainty across training seeds. Data seed 42 and Appendix C.5's ten replications per sample remain unchanged; no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark scores are retained. Table 2 adds AIME/LiveBench Pass@1: T4A4 scores 3.40/6.73 versus T4A1's 2.07/6.59. Table 8 adds Qwen3 T16A1 math accuracy of 17.90 and timings. Tables 12–13 add reward-variability measurements and temperature-0.1 trajectory results, including DFD 178.63. Redisplayed GSM8K/HumanEval values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 follows an approximate variance formula with limits stated for the variance itself. v4 Definition 3.1 and Section 3.3 formalize generic shared contexts, explicitly define conditional first-order estimation variance, add positivity, boundedness, and non-outlier assumptions, and restrict the variance-floor and monotonicity conclusions accordingly. Appendix C.4 also qualifies the answer-variance expression as a formal growing-dimension analogue rather than a rigorous fixed-dimension delta-method result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion recast the contribution as a shared-context principle instantiated by GRPO-MA. Claims of empirical necessity and strictly superior performance are narrowed to effectiveness, potential necessity within the stated estimator setting, and matching or slightly outperforming thought scaling. The claim of the first variance-based analysis is removed.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive qualifications about approximation error, residual correlations, breakpoint effectiveness, and validation at only the thought–answer boundary. It explains temperature changes as changing the estimation target, interprets weaker Pass@1 gains on difficult benchmarks through sparse rewards, and adds an interpretation distinguishing the roles of CoT and branching in manipulation.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly states N=10 for GSM8K/HumanEval, Table 8 reports Qwen3 seconds per training step, and Appendices G.6–G.7 document sampling temperatures and reward normalization for the new diagnostics. The existing hardware, software, prompts, and Appendix E hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Oehlert (1992) and Appendix C.6's explicit mapping of TreePO, TreeRL, and TreeRPO into the shared-context framework, while positioning GRPO-MA more clearly as an explanatory instantiation. Most cited research is retained; the Chen reference consolidation and GTPO bibliographic update concern existing works.

P1.justification: v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, theory narrative, and conclusion. It merges the separate preliminaries and method sections into Method and Analysis, placing the generic framework and analysis before the GRPO-MA instantiation. Terminology and appendix organization are revised, and conflict-of-interest, acknowledgement, and publication text are added.

P2.justification: Table 2 is expanded and reorganized, Table 8 gains a comparator row and timing column, and Tables 9, 12, and 13 are added. Tables 3–4 change their bolding conventions for near-ties. Existing Figures 1–18 retain their graphics, with relocation and limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially improves the reliability of the central theoretical argument by replacing v3's exact-sounding variance and necessity conclusions with explicitly conditional first-order results, stated regularity conditions, and clearer applicability limits. The reward-variance and temperature checks and Qwen3 thought-scaling comparison strengthen empirical support. These gains outweigh a localized new reporting inconsistency: Table 8 prints a T16A1 code score despite its caption saying that run was omitted.
